sentences.text: This tiny creature weighed less than one kilogram, making it one of the smallest non-avian dinosaurs known to science.
It is distinguished by the complete fusion of its ankle bones to other leg structures, a feature absent in other members of its family.
The species Albinykus baatar was formally named by Nesbitt, Clarke, Turner, and Norell in 2011.
This genus was established by the same team of researchers during that year.
The sitting posture of the holotype resembles that of birds, suggesting a close evolutionary link between non-avian maniraptoran dinosaurs and modern birds.
Scientists remain unsure how the holotype died in its preserved position, though it is possible it suffocated under sand.
The animal belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae.
It is classified within the suborder Theropoda.
Albinykus lived from the Santonian to the Campanian stages, between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.
Fossils have been recovered from the Santonian-aged Javkhlant Formation in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.
